scope: Pedagogical exemplars, not verbatim textbook tasks
sourcePolicy: No example contains verified textbook answers, quotes, transcripts, source timecodes or page mappings. Do not publish until teacher maps and verifies actual input.

examples.aim: Infer a lesson topic using visible photo evidence.

steps.instruction: Look at the photograph. Write down two things you can see.
steps.scaffold: I can see … / There is …
steps.check: Compare observations against the photo; do not guess unseen details.
steps.transition: Use your observations to make a supported guess.

steps.instruction: Use one visual clue to predict what today's lesson may be about.
steps.scaffold: I think the lesson is about … because I can see …
steps.check: Can the learner point to the cited clue?

steps.instruction: Tell your partner your prediction and reason. Ask what clue they noticed.
steps.scaffold: What makes you think that? / I noticed …
steps.check: Both learners speak; transition to the real unit title.
steps.transition: Connect predictions with the verified unit focus.

examples.aim: Understand, pronounce and use selected words in context.

steps.instruction: Look at the picture. Match each supplied word to an object or action you can identify.
steps.scaffold: I think … means … because …
steps.check: Review against verified image/context; do not auto-invent distractors.

steps.instruction: Compare your matches. Practise each word and mark its stressed syllable.
steps.scaffold: The stress is on … / It means …
steps.check: Teacher confirms meaning and pronunciation from approved source.

steps.instruction: Choose two words and write one true sentence about your life with each.
steps.scaffold: I usually … / I sometimes …
steps.check: Peer checks meaning; teacher checks context and form.
steps.transition: Recycle target words in next task.

examples.aim: Discover form and meaning, then use the target pattern accurately.

steps.instruction: Read the supplied examples. Underline the repeated grammar pattern and circle the words around it.
steps.scaffold: I notice … comes before/after …
steps.check: Teacher verifies highlights against the source.
steps.transition: Form a rule from the examples.

steps.instruction: Explain to your partner what the pattern means and when it is used. Write one rule together.
steps.scaffold: We use … when … / The form is …
steps.check: Teacher shows verified rule only after hypotheses.
steps.transition: Apply the pattern to original questions.

steps.instruction: Complete the original textbook exercise. Explain one choice using the rule.
steps.scaffold: I chose … because the subject/meaning is …
steps.check: Teacher checks with source-verified keys; no model-created key.

steps.instruction: Tell your partner two true sentences using the target pattern. Ask one follow-up question.
steps.scaffold: I … / What about you?
steps.output: Two spoken examples and a follow-up
steps.check: Partner gives specific feedback on target form.

examples.aim: Reconstruct meaning of the reading and justify original textbook answers.
sourceRequirements: teacher-verified evidence locator for each answer

steps.instruction: Read only your assigned section. Write two main ideas and one supporting detail.
steps.scaffold: My section is mainly about … / One detail is …
steps.output: Two ideas plus one text-based detail
steps.check: Learner underlines where each idea came from.

steps.instruction: Meet classmates with the same section. Agree on the three points everyone must teach.
steps.scaffold: Our most important point is … because paragraph …
steps.output: Three agreed points and a text locator
steps.check: Each member must explain at least one point.

steps.instruction: Return to your home group. Teach your section, listen to each member and complete your group notes.
steps.scaffold: My section explains … / Could you repeat …?
steps.check: Group reporter checks all sections are represented.

steps.instruction: Answer the original textbook questions. For each answer, locate the supporting text and explain why it fits.
steps.scaffold: The evidence is in … / It supports the answer because …
steps.check: Teacher reveals only verified item-level answer/evidence/why.
steps.transition: Reflect on what helped locate the evidence.

examples.aim: Complete the authentic listening task and justify choices using actually heard clues.
sourceRequirements: checked transcript or teacher-reviewed audio evidence

steps.instruction: Read the original task and match the supplied key phrases to likely places or meanings. Record one prediction.
steps.scaffold: I expect to hear … because …
steps.output: One recorded prediction or matching sheet
steps.check: Compare predictions; no claim that the audio has been heard.

steps.instruction: Listen once. Answer each original question independently before speaking to anyone.
steps.scaffold: Question 1: … / Question 2: …
steps.check: Keep attempts visible for later comparison.

steps.instruction: Listen again. Write the word or phrase you actually heard that supports each answer.
steps.scaffold: I heard … / This suggests …
steps.check: If unclear, mark ? and replay; never fill the transcript by guessing.

steps.instruction: Compare both your answers and heard clues. Circle any item you disagree on.
steps.scaffold: I chose … because I heard … / Can we replay …?
steps.output: Agreed answers plus a replay list
steps.check: Both partners explain a clue; teacher can replay selected clip.

steps.instruction: Check each original question using the teacher's verified answer and audio evidence. Correct your own notes.
steps.scaffold: My answer changed from … to … because …
steps.output: Final checked answers and one justified correction
steps.check: Teacher reveals item-wise only; withhold Evidence/Why if source verification is pending.
steps.transition: Use target language in a short follow-up.

examples.aim: Give a personal opinion and report another person's viewpoint.

steps.instruction: Write one answer to the prompt and two reasons from your own experience.
steps.scaffold: I think … because … / Another reason is …
steps.check: Both reasons must support the learner's own view.

steps.instruction: Tell your partner your view. Ask one follow-up question, then note their answer.
steps.scaffold: Why do you think so? / Can you give an example?
steps.check: Both partners speak and listen, not only read frames.

steps.instruction: Tell the class your partner's idea and one reason. Check with your partner that you understood.
steps.scaffold: My partner thinks … because …
steps.check: Peer confirms accurate reporting; teacher comments on clarity.

examples.aim: Produce and improve an original text meeting the given task and criteria.

steps.instruction: Underline the task requirements and write an outline with one idea per paragraph.
steps.scaffold: Introduction → Main idea → Support → Closing
steps.check: Compare outline to the verified prompt.

steps.instruction: Write your own first draft using the outline; include supporting details.
steps.scaffold: One reason is … / For example …
steps.check: Mark any requirement not yet addressed.

steps.instruction: Use the rubric to identify one strength and one specific improvement in your partner's text.
steps.scaffold: This is clear because … / You could improve … by …
steps.output: One strength and one actionable suggestion
steps.check: Comments refer to a criterion, not just 'good'.

steps.instruction: Revise your draft and highlight two changes you made because of feedback.
steps.scaffold: I changed … to … because …
steps.output: Revised final writing and two marked edits
steps.check: Compare final text to original task and rubric.
